messages:
maria_support: Hey team, just got an escalation from Acme (INC-5421). After last weekend's rollout (canary -> stable for model variant 'redwood-v2-encode'), their generated invoices lost line breaks in addresses, e.g. "123 Main St. Suite 5" becomes "123 Main St. Suite 5" on one line instead of separate address lines. Customer says tiny prompt differences (trailing period/whitespace) now change formatting.

customer_acme: Hi, this started after the model update Saturday. Our invoice templates used to preserve each address component on its own line. Now the street + unit often collapse. Very high priority for billing exports. Screenshot and sample payload attached in ticket.

support-bot: Ticket INC-5421 created, priority P1. Request ID examples: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0f9e8d7c.

maria_support: Repro steps from customer: 1) POST to /v1/generate with model redwood-v2-encode 2) prompt: 
```
Generate an invoice line for the shipping address:\n{{street}}\n{{unit}}\n{{city}}, {{state}} {{zip}}\n```
with street="123 Main St." and unit="Suite 5" 3) Response sometimes returns without the separator/newline between street and unit. They claim adding/removing a trailing period in street toggles behavior.

devon_oncall: Can you paste exact request body and response sample? Also which rollout ID triggered the change?

maria_support: Here's sanitized customer request (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-encode","prompt":"Generate an invoice line for the shipping address:\n123 Main St.\nSuite 5\nPortland, OR 97201","max_tokens":50,"temperature":0.0}'
```
Response body (truncated):
```
"123 Main St. Suite 5\nPortland, OR 97201"
```
Expected:
```
"123 Main St.\nSuite 5\nPortland, OR 97201"
```

alan_ml: Hmm. That smells like a tokenization / detokenization difference or a change in how the model treats newline tokens vs punctuation. Weekend rollout notes: changed prefix-kv cache hash to dedupe trailing whitespace and applied a small tokenizer patch upstream for punctuation joins. Could be that the model started treating period+newline as joinable sequence.

devon_oncall: We should verify: 1) Is this only with redwood-v2-encode or other variants? 2) Is it input-sensitive (trailing space vs no trailing space)? 3) Are cached responses being served from old hot cache?

maria_support: Customer says it started only after they saw our announcement for the stable switch on Sat 03/06. They can reproduce locally against stable but not against the snapshot tagged pre-rollout (redwood-v2-encode@20240328). They provided two request_ids (r-0a1b2c3d, r-0f9e8d7c).

alan_ml: I'm going to run a small eval harness across variants. Can someone drop the exact prompt variants (with/without trailing period and trailing whitespace)?

maria_support: Provided variants: A) "123 Main St.\nSuite 5\n" B) "123 Main St\nSuite 5\n" C) "123 Main St. \nSuite 5\n" (note trailing space after period) D) single-line input "123 Main St. Suite 5\n"

alan_ml: Running quick checks now. If this is tokenizer behavior, quantized kernels or new detokenization heuristics might be different. Also check if prefix/KV caching collides: if prompt ends with a punctuation the runtime might strip or merge newline tokens when reusing cache segments.

devon_oncall: I'll enable request-level debug logging for redwood-v2-encode for the customer's requests and check routing. Also open an internal incident channel if it escalates. Tentative action: rollback stable to pre-rollout tag for a short window if we confirm regressions widespread.

maria_support: I told them we're investigating and will provide patch/mitigation in 4 hours.

alan_ml: Quick results: variant pre-rollout preserves newlines for all variants A/B/C. Stable compresses A and C (where period present) into a single line; B (no period) usually preserves newline. So the presence of period followed by newline seems to trigger join. Sample tokenized sequences show that in stable we map ".\n" -> single token 0x7f while pre-rollout keeps "." and "\n" separate. That mapping change explains behavior.

devon_oncall: That mapping change came from tokenizer upstream bump in our build. Looks like the tokenizer was updated to add a dot+newline merge rule. We need to: 1) Immediately add a runtime detokenize override for dot+newline to expand back to dot + newline 2) Backfill canary with fix and roll to stable OR 3) Provide customer workaround: insert explicit placeholder like "<NL>" between lines and post-process.

maria_support: Customer prefers a server-side fix. They've got many invoice templates; workarounds are costly.

alan_ml: I'll draft a hotfix that adds a post-detokenize pass restoring any occurrence of ".\n" to ".\n" (seems trivial but must ensure no perf regression). I'll bench it in canary and post results.

devon_oncall: Action items:
- @alan_ml: push hotfix to canary (redwood-v2-encode) and run regen suite (30m)
- @devon_oncall: enable debug logging for the provided request IDs and watch for other customers (ongoing)
- @maria_support: update INC-5421 with repro, ETA, and potential rollback window if hotfix fails
- @support-bot: tag as P1 and notify ops if more than 3 customers report similar 

support-bot: Noted. Ops channel will be notified on escalation threshold. :rotating_light:

maria_support: Thanks. Alan, ping here when canary results are in and I'll coordinate customer communication.

alan_ml: Canary run done: hotfix preserves newlines and passes regression harness. No measurable latency impact in microbench. I'll push to stable in staged rollout with a 30m watch and automatic rollback if error rate or latency increases >2x baseline.

devon_oncall: I'll keep an eye on error rates and tokenization logs during the rollout.

maria_support: Customer updated: thanks for quick turnaround, they appreciate the fast response. I'll keep INC-5421 updated and ask them to validate fixed behavior once stable is updated.

customer_acme: Confirmed fix on our side after today's rollout. Newlines preserved. Thanks team! :tada:

maria_support: Closing loop, marking as resolved in ticket after customer confirmation. Will follow up with postmortem describing cause (upstream tokenizer change) and mitigation (add detokenize safety checks + add upstream update gating for template-sensitive endpoints).

devon_oncall: Suggestion for postmortem: add a small suite of template-preservation unit tests (addresses, invoices, legal clauses) to catch this earlier.

alan_ml: Agreed. I'll add tests and a patch to the tokenizer integration checklist.

maria_support: Great. Closing thread.
